bib.title: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks

question: Can an LLM trained with a finite attention window run on infinite-length streams without losing efficiency or quality?
hypothesis: Initial tokens act as attention sinks (softmax must sum to one), so keeping their KV with a sliding window restores performance; a dedicated sink token in pretraining would need only one.
contributions: Identify the attention sink phenomenon and explain window attention failure
StreamingLLM: keep 4 initial tokens' KV plus rolling window, no fine-tuning
Pretrain with a learnable sink token so one token suffices
StreamEval benchmark and 22.2x speedup over recompute baseline

method.summary: StreamingLLM keeps the KV of the first 4 tokens plus a rolling window of recent tokens, with positions assigned by cache slot. Evaluated on perplexity over concatenated PG19, streaming QA, and speed; separately pretrains 160M models with/without a sink token.
method.task: streaming language modeling / KV cache eviction

datasets.name: PG19 test (100 books, concatenated)
datasets.size: 4M+ tokens concatenated; first book 65K tokens; 400K-token subset for Tables 2 and 6

datasets.name: Pile (deduplicated)
datasets.preprocessing: sink token prepended to every training sample in the sink model

datasets.name: ARC-Easy/Challenge
datasets.preprocessing: all QA pairs concatenated into one stream

datasets.name: StreamEval
datasets.size: 100 samples x 100 queries; 23 tokens per line
datasets.preprocessing: query every 10 lines, answer 20 lines prior

models.name: Sink-token 160M models (Vanilla, Zero Sink, Learnable Sink)

training.lr_schedule: kept from Pythia recipe, values not given

other.note: Only the 160M sink-token pretraining trains; StreamingLLM itself needs no fine-tuning

inference.decoding: perplexity (teacher-forced) for LM; exact match for QA
inference.prompting: StreamEval format in Fig 8; ARC questions concatenated

parameters.cache_size: Llama-2 2048, others 1024 (half the pretraining window); QA window/StreamingLLM 1024
parameters.positions: assigned by position in cache, not original text; RoPE keys cached before rotation

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match at each answer position

metrics.name: per-token decoding latency
metrics.definition: ms per token, and memory in GB

eval.protocol: Single runs, no seeds or significance tests stated; latency on single A6000 with HF Transformers

prompts.text: The REGISTER_CONTENT in line 0 is <8806> ... Query: The REGISTER_CONTENT in line 0 is

results.claim: StreamingLLM gives up to 22.2x per-token decoding speedup over sliding window with re-computation, with similar memory
results.setup: Llama-2-7B/13B, single A6000, HF Transformers, cache sizes 256-4096
results.quote:
StreamingLLM achieves an impressive speedup,
reaching up to 22.2× per token.

results.claim: Window attention collapses once the first tokens are evicted: Llama-2-13B PPL 5158.07 at 0+1024 vs 5.40 with 4+1020
results.setup: Llama-2-13B, first PG19 test book (65K tokens), cache 1024

results.claim: Replacing the 4 initial tokens with linebreak tokens still restores perplexity, so position matters more than semantics
Four initial tokens suffice on Llama-2-7B; one or two do not fully recover (cache 4096)
results.setup: Llama-2-7B, 400K tokens concatenated PG19 test, cache 4+4092

results.claim: StreamingLLM models text of more than 4 million tokens with stable perplexity across families
results.setup: Llama-2-[7,13,70]B, Falcon-[7,40]B, Pythia-[2.8,6.9,12]B, MPT-[7,30]B, concatenated PG19 test; Llama-2 cache 2048, others 1024
results.quote:
StreamingLLM can reliably handle exceptionally
extended texts, encompassing more than 4 million tokens

results.claim: With a learnable sink token in pre-training, 1+1023 cache gives streaming perplexity equal to full window
results.setup: 160M model, Pythia recipe, first PG19 sample, cache 1+1023
results.note: Vanilla 1+1023 is 18.49; 0+1024 learnable sink 1235, zero sink 29214

results.claim: Sink token in pretraining does not hurt zero-shot accuracy (e.g. ARC-e 45.6 vs 45.2)
Streaming ARC-Easy on Llama-2-13B-Chat: StreamingLLM beats one-shot; window attention near zero
results.setup: Llama-2-13B-Chat, ARC-E concatenated stream, cache 1024, exact match
results.table: Table 5, row StreamingLLM, column Llama-2-13B-Chat Arc-E

results.claim: Increasing cache size does not consistently lower perplexity (Llama-2-7B 9.08 at 4+2044 vs 9.59 at 4+4092)
StreamEval: Llama-2-7B-32K-Instruct accuracy drops to 0.00 once query-answer distance exceeds cache (4+2044 at 100 lines)
results.setup: StreamEval, 100 samples x 100 queries, 23 tokens per line

results.claim: LongBench: StreamingLLM 4+3496 underperforms truncation (NarrativeQA 11.6 vs 18.7); 1750+1750 restores it
A second sink token gave no gain and the model then needs both: 2 sink tokens at 1+1023 gives 25.73

limits: Does not extend context window or long-term memory; unsuitable for long-document QA and summarization (Appendix A)
Accuracy goes to zero when query-answer distance exceeds cache (Table 7)
Larger cache does not consistently reduce perplexity (Table 6)
Sink-token results are on 160M models only
No seeds or confidence intervals; 2023 HF implementation latency
